items.detail: The **Nasdaq** plunged 5.52% to 24,315.00 Thursday, putting it in a correction, and the S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, its worst day since April 2025.
items.why: Fears that a Democratic Congress will slow data-center construction wiped out Wednesday's post-election rally in AI stocks.

items.detail: Chip stocks led the selloff: the **Philadelphia Semiconductor Index** plunged more than 12%, and memory maker Micron sank about 17%.
items.why: Qualcomm's weak smartphone-chip outlook came on top of election fears about slower spending on AI infrastructure.

items.detail: Friday's **October jobs report** is next, with futures pricing about a 66% chance that the Fed raises rates in December.
items.why: A strong report would make a hike more likely just as tech stocks are already under heavy pressure.

items.detail: South Korea's **Kospi** plunged more than 8% Friday and tripped a circuit breaker, and Taiwan fell over 8% before officials moved to calm investors.
items.why: Wall Street's AI rout hit Asia's big chip suppliers hardest: Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC.

items.detail: The **Nifty** jumped 2.4% to 24,536.60 Thursday, its best day in seven months, then held almost flat Friday while the rest of Asia crashed.
items.why: Cheaper crude and foreign buying drove the rally, and IT stocks rose on hopes that slower AI spending helps them.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell 4.4% to 2,729.89 Thursday, about as much as the S&P 500, as the AI selloff spread beyond the biggest stocks.
items.why: Smaller companies tied to the data-center build-out were sold along with chipmakers on fears of slower AI spending.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** fell about 6% to near $75,700 Thursday, wiping out Wednesday's post-election bounce above $80,000.
items.why: The Wall Street tech rout spilled into crypto, forcing more than $1 billion of leveraged bets to close.

items.detail: **Ether** dropped 7.8% to about **$2,234** Thursday, giving back all of Wednesday's 5% rebound.
items.why: The tech selloff hit as US spot ether ETFs posted a seventh straight day of outflows.

items.detail: **Solana** fell 6.3% to about **$89.90**, testing its 200-day average for the first time since August.
items.why: About $34 million of bullish bets were forced to close as the stock rout spread, with no ETF inflows to cushion it.

items.detail: **Gold** rose nearly 2% to about $4,100 Thursday, a two-week high and back above $4,000, after Wednesday's 3.4% jump.
items.why: The dollar sank to its lowest since September 30 and Treasury yields fell after the Democratic wins.

crossCuttingTheme: Fears that a Democratic Congress will slow AI data-center spending turned into a full rout: chips led Wall Street's worst day since April 2025, Asia's chip-heavy markets and crypto followed, while a falling dollar and yields lifted gold.
